newsitem.title: UK: WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUGUST 11.
newsitem.headline: WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUGUST 11.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - Grey Advertising Inc says it has been chosen by HFS Inc to be its agency of record for its $100 million multi-media account encompassing HFS's hotel/motel chains, including the Ramada, Days Inn, Super 8, Howard Johnson, Knights Inn, Villager Lodge and Wingate Inn chains.

LONDON - True North Communications Inc , the U.S.-based advertising holding company, which is expanding its global network with its recently announced purchase of Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon and Eckhardt Inc, is expected to remain on the acquisition trail to further beef up its European presence, industry sources said.
BERLIN - Berlin-based advertising agency Dorland says it expects a 20 percent boost in turnover for 1997, propelled by publicity generated by its recent capture of Honda's German image account.

DENVER - Tele-Communications Inc is spending about $100 million on marketing in the second half of the year in order to win back customers from direct broadcast satellite, President and Chief Operating Officer Leo Hindery says.

PARIS - France's billboard firms are using the slogan "Freedom of speech began on walls" for a campaign aimed at highlighting their role in giving free space to charities and good causes. The campaign was devised by advertising agency Alice, part of Interpublic Group's Lowe Group, for the billboard owners' association, Union de la Publicite Exterieur.

MUNICH - The German computer and software industry doubled spending on advertising between 1993 and 1996 to 227 million marks ($122.8 million), largely due to consumers' constant demand for information about new products, media marketing firm MediaGruppe Muenchen (MGM) reports.

LONDON - British companies are dipping into their pockets to support charitable causes not only in a spirit of altruism, but to improve their image and boost sales, industry experts say. "Cause-related marketing", the promotion of a brand in conjunction with a good cause such as a charity, is growing as companies seek new ways to win customers.

KRONBERG, Germany - TMM-Turkmedia, a unit of media marketing company IP Deutschland, drops ad prices on its Turkish-language channel TRT International an average of 10 percent compared to this year's rates. Kanal D, another of the company's stations, raises ad prices 28 percent.

PARIS - Advertising revenue at M6, France's second biggest private terrestrial television station, rose to 1.08 billion francs ($173.4 million) in the six months to June 30 from 999.1 million in the first half of 1996, the company says in the official Balo bulletin.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - British publishing group EMAP Plc says it has bought Australian firms Mason Stewart Publishing and Bounty Services for a total of five million pounds ($7.9 million). "We believe there is further potential for our magazines in Australia," the company says.

LONDON - Britain's Independent Television Commission says it is investigating whether the wholesale price discount structure for British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc's premium channels could prevent the entry of other providers into the market, following a complaint from cable companies.

LONDON - British commercial radio increased its share of the country's listening audience to 50.2 percent in the 1997 second quarter, nearly three percentage points ahead of the BBC radio stations, a radio trade group says. In addition, the Radio Advertising Bureau says commercial radio posted record quarterly revenue figures in the second quarter, up 13.3 percent year-on-year to 87.5 million pounds.

MADRID - Spain's Via Digital says it is in talks with DirecTV, the satellite television division of giant Hughes Electronics, regarding the purchase of a significant stake in the digital television platform.

LONDON - Britain's national daily newspapers continue to battle for market share, with rivals the Daily Telegraph and the Times both posting gains in the six months from February to July, the Audit Bureau of Circulation says.

CANBERRA - The Australian government may announce changes to the cross-media ownership laws within the next few days, a government official says. The issue is on the agenda to be considered by the Cabinet on Tuesday.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

INGOLSTADT, Germany - Audi AG, the luxury carmaker, says pre-tax profits climbed 20.9 percent in the first half of this year to 489 million marks, driven by strong foreign demand. Audi says group sales increased 13.7 percent during the first half of the year to 10.6 billion marks -- an increase that analysts said came largely on the back of its mainstay A4 saloon.

TOKYO - International Business Machines Corp's Japan unit says the company will cut wholesale prices of home-use personal computers by 10 to 15 percent across-the-board. The cutback reflects lower prices for Intel Corp's Pentium microprocessors, an IBM Japan spokesman says.

NEW DELHI - Multinational companies rushing into India to grab a chunk of the market are ignoring the pitfalls of selling in a nation as large as much of Europe -- and a great deal poorer, say advertising agencies. "You want to sell in India, you've got to sell at Indian prices," says Sandeep Goyal, executive vice president of advertising agency Rediffusion-Dentsu, Young and Rubicam.

BONN - Germany's traditional two-week summer sales period gets mixed reviews from some of the country's major department stores as poor weather and worries about the economy weigh on sales in some regions.

DALLAS - Seeking to distinguish itself in a hotly competitive field, PrimeCo Personal Communications of Westlake, Texas, launches a major marketing effort to develop a brand name in wireless phone service.

DUBLIN - Ireland's Minister for Enterprise, Trade and Employment Mary Harney approves the proposed merger between Avonmore Foods and Waterford Foods, paving the way for the creation of the world's fourth largest milk processor and the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LOS ANGELES - Memphis, Tennessee, is bracing itself as millions of fans prepare to mark the 20th anniversary of Elvis Presley's death in what is billed as the biggest Elvis extravaganza ever. There will be Elvis riverboat cruises and dance parties as well as the ongoing cottage industry of kitsch that sells everything from 35-cent postcards to $12,000 jukeboxes -- with the King's face on every item.

BEIJING - China has become Asia's largest ostrich breeding country with a total of 80,000 birds in its farms, including 15,000 fledglings, the People's Daily Overseas Edition says. China is hoping to make ostrich meat into a popular part of the Chinese diet.
